page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 virtual CPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It operates on a KVM hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10% to 25% categories. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth tests show average read and write speeds, though the PassMark memory score is positioned in the lower 25%. The instance handles database operations and Redis SET operations with average throughput, achieving 11.3 million operations per second in Redis testing.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1.4xlarge offers a high-density memory configuration relative to its compute resources. This allows organizations to run memory-intensive workloads without incurring the costs associated with higher vCPU tiers. Given the lack of local storage and GPUs, this instance is best suited for memory-bound applications such as in-memory caching, database operations, static web serving, and moderate multi-threaded processing tasks that do not require high single-core clock speeds.
